[agent-bulk] Vertex judged from the event's own +-111.6 cm sweep (event_half_span_cm 111.6, under the 150 cm trigger, so no --vtx-span re-capture). VERDICT on 6013 (349.8 MeV, 7 seg, table length 140.1 cm, the leading shower): over-clustered. Three reasons. (1) Its start is at dist 0.0 from the nu vertex and its seed is in cluster 6, the SAME cluster as the muon 6009 which ends on that vertex -- a converted photon cannot start on the vertex; this is the pilot's evt280159 signature (a vertex blob seeded on the muon stem), here much larger. (2) Its yellow member set does not read as one cone from one apex: in BOTH azimuths (az-055 and az+085) the members trace a closed circuit around a largely empty quadrilateral, and the axis arrow points in a direction that matches almost none of the member bulk. The chain is 6013 -> 6017 -> 6019 -> 6020 with 6021 as a stub: 129 cm of skeleton path inside a spatial extent of only about 40x60x20 cm, and 6017 alone is 51.3 cm of polyline between two endpoints that are 12.8 cm apart. (3) The member set runs from the vertex all the way back to (-120,165,236), which is 15 cm from the muon's OTHER end (-115,168,250) and sits in the same region as the separate shower 6015 -- so cluster 6's far end is split between two showers while 6013 spans the whole cluster. It also swallows 50027 (pdg 13) and 54031 (pdg 2212). NO MARKS on 6013: like the pilot on evt280159 I could not name which segments to remove with confidence -- the member chain is contiguous and I cannot say where the real shower ends and the cluster-traversal begins. SECOND SHOWER 70063 (339.4 MeV, 11 seg) is the opposite and is the most photon-like object in the event: detached (closest member 41 cm from the vertex), all 11 members from_vertices walk_add at 0-28.6 cm and 2.8-21.2 deg, and in 3-D it starts narrow at its X and opens into a multi-branch fan with a dense point cloud. It IS mildly under-clustered: shw70063-acc shows four non-member circles inside or on the pass-1 box, and the shower's own choices are internally inconsistent -- it absorbed 60037 at 44.9 cm / 16.3 deg by pass4_angle but left 63040 at 47.1 cm / 6.3 deg (tier 1, 8.4 MeV) and 66043 at 25.4 cm / 2.8 deg (tier 1, 7.8 MeV), both at SMALLER angle. MARKS on 70063: 66043 IN (strongest -- 2.8 deg, 25 cm, tier 1), 63040 IN (47.1 cm, 6.3 deg, tier 1), 69062 IN (32.6 cm, 25.3 deg, weakest of the three on geometry alone but see the pi0 argument). Per correction 11 none of these three is truly grey: each heads its own trivial 8-17 MeV shower, so this is the weaker class of under-clustering evidence; I did not mark 58035 (46.0 cm, 12.8 deg) because it IS a member of 66043's shower and would come along with it. Total marked-in charge about 33 MeV on 339.4, i.e. 10%. PI0 -- THE MAIN FINDING, and I dispute the reconstruction's pairing. Reco group 0 is 6013 + 69062, stored mass 118.3 MeV, asymmetry 0.91. gamma1 is the vertex-attached blob above (start dist 0.0 from the vertex), so it cannot be a converted photon. gamma2 is a single 16.6 MeV segment sitting 6.2 cm from shower 70063's members. I priced the alternatives with --pio-pairs (shots-pio/evt98844): 70063+69062 gives theta 39.9 deg (axis) / 9.4 deg (VERTEX convention) -> m 51.2 / 12.3 MeV. A 9.4 deg opening angle from the vertex is not two photons; it is one photon and a fragment of itself, which is the quantitative reason 69062 is marked into 70063 rather than paired with anything. The other alternatives are all far off the pi0 mass: 70063+65042 = 247.7 / 234.4 MeV, 70063+6015 = 245.2 / 250.9 MeV, 70063+71064 = 60.7 (axis) / 179.5 (vertex). So there is NO credible pi0 pairing in this event among the in-scope showers, and I stored none. The reco's 118.3 MeV group 0 should be treated as a pairing of a vertex blob with a fragment of another shower. In the 3-D view at az-055-el+20 AND again at az-055-el+65 the yellow member set is ONE long, thin, perfectly straight line of uniform width running about 140 cm from the X to a small hook at the far end -- no cone, no widening, no branching anywhere along it. [agent-bulk] The nuecc of my shard, and the reconstruction handles it WELL. Vertex judged from a --vtx-span 60 re-capture (event_half_span_cm 357.1 -- correction 5). NOTE ON A HEURISTIC I USED ELSEWHERE AND DELIBERATELY DID NOT USE HERE: on evt98844 and evt58006 I argued 'start at dist 0.0 from the vertex, therefore not a converted photon'. A nuecc PRIMARY ELECTRON starts at the vertex, so that argument is void on this event and I did not apply it, even though both 11032 and 11035 have dvtx 0.0. VERDICT on 11032 (562.4 MeV, 30 segments, 109.1 cm): correct. In the 3-D view at az-055-el+20 AND again at az+085-el+20 the member set is one cone from one apex with the right internal structure for a high-energy electron: a narrow MIP-like stem for the first ~35 cm out of the X, then a visible widening into a branching fan, then a diffuse cloud of small fragments out to ~90 cm. The axis arrow lies along that development in both views. 562 MeV is about 6-7 X0 of visible shower, so members out to 92 cm are appropriate, not excessive. The reconstruction has assembled 30 segments drawn from roughly 20 DIFFERENT clusters into that one object -- this is the case where the pass3_cone / pass4 machinery is doing exactly what it should, and it is worth recording as a positive alongside my over-clustering calls elsewhere in this shard. UNDER-CLUSTERING is negligible and I measured it: the acceptance plot shows only three non-member circles, at 64.3 cm / 31.9 deg (35050, 1.9 MeV, outside the 25 deg cone), 82.6 cm / 22.5 deg (55070, 1.3 MeV) and 83.3 cm / 15.8 deg (52067, 1.6 MeV). The last two are the by-now familiar 'just outside the 80 cm pass-1 box' pair, but here they total 2.9 MeV against 562.4, i.e. 0.5 percent, so I did NOT mark them -- naming them as a defect would misrepresent the scale. Note the shower did reach past 80 cm on its own at small angle (49064 at 84.6 cm / 1.8 deg and 50065 at 91.9 cm / 5.3 deg, both tier 2, pass3_cone), so the 80 cm box is not a hard stop here. OVER-CLUSTERING: the member list contains many pdg 13 and pdg 2212 labels (37052, 39054, 42057, 43058, 45060, 48063, 53068, 56071, 70074, 72079, 73080 ...), but every one of them is a 2-6 point speck inside a 562 MeV shower's fragment cloud, where a per-segment PID is meaningless; I do not read them as foreign objects. SECOND SHOWER 11035 (110.0 MeV, 3 seg) is the other prong: its own 18.5 cm segment out of the vertex plus two pdg-13 2-point specks, 30045 and 34049, absorbed by pass3_cone at 63 and 71 cm on its side of the event. I did not scrutinise it further and record no verdict for it. NOT looked at: the 19 showers the scope rule skipped, all under 4 MeV except that some are the fragments discussed above. No pi0: no reco group, all in-scope pio_id -1; the pio-*.png is the capture's auto pair (11032+11035) and both of those start ON the vertex with a 413.3 MeV axis-convention mass, so it is not a pi0 and I propose none. drag_check live: probe_radius_px 334, seg_u 350.16 -> 277.24, cloud_u 74.53 -> 101.68, cloud_redrew true.

A DENSITY READING I CHECKED AND THEN WITHDREW, worth recording because it nearly produced a wrong flag: 112.4 MeV over a 9.2 cm skeleton is 12 MeV/cm, which would be far above MIP and would have read as a proton. But in the 3-D view at az-055 the point spray above the X extends roughly three times further than the skeletonised segment (about 30 cm against 9 cm), so the charge is spread over the spray and the real density is about 3.7 MeV/cm -- shower-like. The lesson is that kine_charge is blob charge and the table's `length` is skeleton length, and dividing one by the other overstates density whenever the skeleton under-covers the blob. I flag it here because I used the same MeV/cm argument on evt53658 and evt105074 in this shard, and on those two it was supported by the 3-D picture (a straight uniform narrow line), whereas here it is not.
